extracted.intended_audience: journalism and communication students, faculty, and anyone creating journalistic infographics or data-driven journalism
extracted.subtask_description: A university library resource guide listing websites, blogs, books, and tools for producing and studying infographics and data visualizations used in journalism. It aims to help learners find examples, tutorials, and visualization software.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summarize complexity into easily digested charts
rubrics_metrics.description: Has an uncanny knack for summing up complicated matters in easily digested charts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied quality: an effective infographic reduces complex subject matter into clear, compact charts that readers can quickly understand (example cited: ChartGirl).

rubrics_metrics.name: Show — don't tell (visual storytelling)
rubrics_metrics.description: Visualjournalism.com is a project to put forward the importance of ‘show – don’t tell’ in modern journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principle: use visuals to demonstrate and narrate rather than relying solely on exposition; prioritize visual evidence and story-telling through imagery and data presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use pictures to tell stories (news aesthetics)
rubrics_metrics.description: News Aesthetics — a blog about how pictures tell stories. Infographics and photography in print and online media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: design infographics so that images/graphics carry narrative weight and convey the story arc or main point without heavy accompanying text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present useful information for quick absorption
rubrics_metrics.description: The goal of the Useful Charts site is to present useful information in the form of study charts so that students, teachers or simply those interested in increasing their general knowledge can absorb the information quickly and visually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: prioritize usefulness and rapid comprehension — charts should be designed to make key facts and relationships immediately perceptible to the target audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model work on high-quality examples and showcases
rubrics_metrics.description: Collections and showcases (Cool Infographics, Infographics Showcase, Infographic Journal) highlight the best examples of data visualizations and infographics found in magazines, newspapers and on the Internet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: consult curated showcases and exemplary work as models for layout, narrative flow, accuracy, and aesthetic standards when producing infographics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose appropriate data visualization tools and resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Listings of visualization tools and resources (DailyTekk, Data visualization-Tools for News, Datavisualization.ch Selected Tools, Over 100 Incredible Infographic Tools and Resources).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical criterion: select tools that fit the data, distribution medium (print/web/mobile), and skill level; the guide points to categorized tool lists and recommendations for practitioners.
